messages:
Elaine: heads-up, CI alert flagged a deploy service account that got an unexpected cluster-admin binding during a canary rollout. digging in now.
Jon: ugh, which canary? stack/name?
Elaine: canary: inference-dedicated-v2, namespace: inference-canary. appears to be a leftover ClusterRoleBinding created by a migration job.
Priya: do we have the binding YAML or audit log entry? can you paste the kubectl output?
Elaine: pasted below from the canary cluster: ```
$ kubectl get clusterrolebinding deploy-canary-sa -o yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: deploy-canary-sa
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy
  namespace: inference-canary
```
Elaine: audit log shows it was created at 2026-03-18T14:12:02Z by a controller pod: infra-migration-job-5f7b.
Matt: that migration job should never create cluster-admin bindings. likely a legacy toggle.
Priya: can we see the audit log record for the user/principal that performed the POST? need the KMS envelope wrap info too, if any.
Elaine: audit entry: "userIdentity": {"systemUser":"infra-migration-sa","source":"k8s"}, requestURI: "/apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/clusterrolebindings" method: POST. No KMS interaction in that call itself.
security-bot: automated note: matched policy: rbac-high-privilege-creation. Ticket created SEC-2026-113.
Jon: first step: remove the ClusterRoleBinding from the canary cluster and replace with Role + RoleBinding scoped to the namespace with the minimal verbs. can anyone run the removal?
Matt: I can do the delete and create a namespaced RoleBinding to allow deploy SA only the required verbs (get, list, watch, create jobs).
Priya: before deleting, snapshot audit logs + who/when for compliance. we need an evidence bundle for the SOC report. Elaine, can you collect the audit files for the 24h window and drop them in the secure bucket? note: use kms-key:projects/redwood-kms/keys/audit-archive for server-side encryption.
Elaine: on it. I'll export /var/log/k8s/audit/* for 2026-03-17..2026-03-19 and upload to gs://redwood-sec-audit/inference-canary/2234567801/ (kms: audit-archive).
Priya: also check if deploy tokens were used outside the canary. search for impersonation or token exchange events and for KMS decrypt requests around that timeframe.
Jon: question: why did infra-migration-sa have permission to create clusterrolebindings? we should trace its role bindings in the management cluster.
Matt: quick check: infra-migration-sa is bound to a ClusterRole called infra-mgr which was granted broad perms during a one-off migration in 2024. I propose we split infra-mgr into infra-mgr-controller (namespace-limited) and infra-mgr-admin (explicit elevated, protected).
Priya: agreed. until we refactor, add a Deny policy (OPA constraint) to block creation of ClusterRoleBinding by infra-migration-sa and similar non-operator SAs. temporary guardrail.
security-bot: OPA constraint applied: deny-clusterrolebinding-creation-by-non-ops, scope=canary, status=applied.
Elaine: I removed the clusterrolebinding at 2026-03-18T15:02:11Z: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding deploy-canary-sa` and created a RoleBinding scoped to inference-canary with minimal permissions.
Matt: nice. can you paste the RoleBinding?
Elaine: created `inference-deploy-limited` RoleBinding referencing Role `inference-deploy-role` with verbs [get,list,watch,create,patch] on pods,deployments,cronjobs.
Priya: let's checkpoint mitigations: 1) snapshot + upload audits (Elaine) 2) OPA deny in canary (Priya) 3) plan for infra-mgr role split (Matt) 4) rotate infra-migration-sa token and revoke active sessions (Jon).
Jon: rotation done at 2026-03-18T15:20Z. I revoked token via the KMS envelope revoke flow and removed the old secret from Vault.
Elaine: quick note: audit shows one kube-apiserver accept where the request was signed by infra-migration-sa from runner-ip 35.243.11.9. that runner belonged to a CI job that was re-used across projects.
Matt: that runner should be quarantined. opsbot, can you block that runner IP at the firewall and create an incident record?
opsbot: firewall rule applied to block 35.243.11.9 at 2026-03-18T15:28:03Z. Incident INC-8472 created and linked to SEC-2026-113.
Priya: follow-up: check KMS audit (who requested decrypt of any deploy secrets) — if the migration job used a wrapped key to push the binding, we need that trace.
Elaine: KMS audit shows no decrypts by infra-migration-sa in that window. however, Vault shows a read of secret path `secret/ci/inference-canary/deploy-token` by the CI pipeline user at 2026-03-18T14:10Z.
Jon: that indicates the CI pipeline likely held the token used by the migration job. we need to enforce ephemeral short-lived tokens for CI runners and bind them to job scopes.
Matt: action items: add TTL max 1h for CI service tokens; ensure Vault role has bound CIDR; add token binding to KMS envelope audits.
Priya: also add a regression test in the infra-ci that asserts no job can create ClusterRoleBinding. include a fake create that should be denied.
security-bot: test plan added to SEC-2026-113: infra-ci regression for RBAC-create-deny.
Elaine: final comment: we'll schedule the infra-mgr role split next sprint, and in the short term will push org-wide notification and a ticket for other repos that used the migration job. please ping here once you complete respective tasks. :white_check_mark:
Jon: noted. I'll follow up after revocation checks and the Canary rollback verification.
Matt: I'll open the PR to split infra-mgr and include migration notes + required approval for infra-mgr-admin.
Priya: I'll prepare the compliance evidence package and update the SOC runbook with the new quarantine steps.
Elaine: thanks all. closing the live triage for now, leaving SEC-2026-113 open until postmortem and role-split complete. :lock:
security-bot: automated: thread archived to SEC-2026-113 after 2h of inactivity.
